name: Bhopal
tagline: City of lakes, nawabi kitchens and two World Heritage Sites an hour away.
intro: Bhopal grew around an 11th-century lake and later became a princely state ruled for over a century by women, the Begums. Spend a day on the lakes and the hilltop museums of Shyamla Hills, an evening eating through the Old City, and a day out to the rock paintings of Bhimbetka or the stupas of Sanchi.

facts.best_time: October to March. April to June regularly crosses 40°C.
facts.getting_there: Raja Bhoj Airport is about 15 km from the centre. Bhopal Junction and Rani Kamlapati stations are on the Delhi–Mumbai and Delhi–Chennai lines.
facts.getting_around: App cabs and autos are easy to find. Agree the fare or use the meter before you set off.
facts.languages: Hindi; English is understood in hotels, museums and most shops.

emergency.label: Police, fire, ambulance
emergency.note: National emergency number, works from any phone

safety_tips: The Boat Club and VIP Road stretches of the Upper Lake stay busy until late. The far lake edges are unlit and empty after dark.
Old City lanes around Chowk get very crowded in the evening. Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket.
Leave Bhimbetka and Sanchi by late afternoon. The roads run through forest and get dark early in winter.
Between April and June, plan outdoor sights for early morning and carry water.

places.name: Upper Lake (Bada Talab)
places.summary: The 11th-century lake credited to Raja Bhoj that gave Bhopal its nickname. Take a boat out from the Boat Club, then walk the lakeside promenade at sunset.

hours.text: Promenade open all day; boating in daylight hours

tips: Boats leave from the Boat Club on Lake Drive Road.
The Shyamla Hills road above the lake has the best views.
places.safety: Stay on the lit Boat Club and VIP Road stretches after dark. The far edges of the lake are isolated.

places.name: Taj-ul-Masajid
places.summary: One of the largest mosques in India, with pink sandstone towers and a huge courtyard. Building started under Shah Jahan Begum in the 19th century and finished in the 1980s.

hours.note: Avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday.

tips: Dress modestly. Women are asked to cover their heads.
Photography is fine, but ask before photographing people at prayer.
places.safety: Busy area with heavy traffic at the gates. Cross with care.

places.name: Madhya Pradesh Tribal Museum
places.summary: Walk-through rooms built by tribal artists from across the state: houses, shrines, a forest of clay figures. Many visitors call it the best museum in the city.
tips: Allow at least two hours.
Chinhari, the museum shop, sells tribal crafts at fair prices.
places.safety: Well staffed and safe. Shyamla Hills roads are quiet at night, so book your cab before leaving.

places.name: Museum of Mankind (IGRMS)
places.summary: An open-air museum of real-size village houses from across India, spread over a hillside above the lake, plus an indoor gallery of folk and tribal life.

hours.note: Closes at 17:30 from March to August.

tips: Wear walking shoes. The trail is long and hilly.
Carry water; there is little shade on the open-air trail.
places.safety: Large, quiet grounds. Keep to the marked trail and leave before closing.

places.name: Van Vihar National Park
places.summary: A small national park on the lake shore where rescued tigers, leopards, bears and crocodiles live in large open enclosures. Cycle or drive the single road through it.

hours.note: Hours shift with the season. Also closed on Holi and Diwali.

fee.indian: ₹25 on foot; more by cycle or vehicle
fee.foreign: Higher rate, ask at the gate

places.best: Early morning, when animals are active
tips: Rent a cycle at the gate.
There are two gates; Chikoo Dwar on Lake View Road is the main one.
places.safety: Stay on the main road and don't feed animals. Exit through a gate before closing; don't walk out along the lake edge.

places.name: Bharat Bhavan
places.summary: An arts centre by architect Charles Correa, built down a hillside towards the lake. It has galleries of modern and tribal art, plus theatre, music and poetry evenings.
places.best: Late afternoon, then stay for an evening show
tips: Check the notice board for performances that evening.
places.safety: Safe and staffed. Combine with the Tribal Museum nearby.

places.name: Gohar Mahal
places.summary: An 1820 palace built by Qudsia Begum, Bhopal's first woman ruler, mixing Hindu and Mughal styles. It now hosts craft fairs and exhibitions.

hours.text: Daytime; opening depends on the fair or exhibition

places.best: During a craft fair (often in winter)
tips: Ask locally whether a mela is on before you go.
places.safety: Old City traffic is heavy. Walk with care around the lake road.

places.name: Shaukat Mahal and Sadar Manzil
places.summary: Two 19th-century palaces at the entrance to the Old City. Shaukat Mahal mixes Gothic and Islamic details; Sadar Manzil was the Begums' hall of public audience.

hours.text: Seen from outside; best in daylight

places.best: Late afternoon, before eating in the Old City
tips: Walk from here into Chowk Bazaar.

places.name: Chowk Bazaar
places.summary: The Old City's market lanes, selling zari-embroidered purses, silver jewellery, bangles and dry fruit around the Jama Masjid.

hours.text: Late morning to late evening; busiest after 18:00

places.best: Early evening, then dinner at Chatori Gali
tips: Bargain politely; start at about half the first price.
Look for jari-batua, Bhopal's embroidered purses.
places.safety: Very crowded lanes. Keep valuables in a front pocket and stay with your group.

places.name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple (Birla Mandir)
places.summary: A hilltop temple with views over the Lower Lake and city, and a small museum of sculpture from the region.

hours.text: Morning and evening darshan; closed for a few hours around midday

tips: Leave shoes at the counter before entering.
places.safety: Safe and busy in the evenings.

places.name: Sanchi Stupa
places.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site: Buddhist stupas, monasteries and four carved gateways from the 3rd century BCE onwards, on a quiet hilltop.

hours.note: Sunrise to sunset. The ASI museum at the foot of the hill is closed on Fridays.

places.best: Early morning, about an hour's drive from Bhopal
tips: Hire a guide at the gate to read the gateway carvings.
Book tickets online at the ASI site to skip the queue.
places.safety: Little shade on the hilltop. Carry water and a hat.

places.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
places.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site: rock shelters in the forest with paintings of hunters, dancers and animals, some of them thousands of years old.
places.best: Morning; combine with Bhojpur on the way back
tips: Follow the numbered trail; the Zoo Rock shelter has the densest paintings.
Monkeys are bold. Keep food in your bag.
places.safety: Forest area with weak mobile signal. Stay on the marked trail and leave well before dark.

places.name: Bhojeshwar Temple, Bhojpur
places.summary: An unfinished 11th-century Shiva temple with one of the largest stone lingams in India. The ramp used to raise its stones can still be traced nearby.
places.best: On the way back from Bhimbetka
tips: Very busy on Mahashivratri. Pick another day unless you want the festival.
places.safety: Rural roads. Travel back to Bhopal before dark.

food.name: Chatori Gali
food.known_for: Bhopal's food lane: paya soup, nihari, seekh kebabs and biryani, open until late.

food.name: Suleimani chai stalls
food.known_for: Bhopal's salty, milky tea. Have a cup after dinner in the Old City.

food.name: Manohar Dairy and Restaurant
food.known_for: A city institution since 1970: poha-jalebi breakfasts, chaat, lassi and sweets.

food.name: Bapu ki Kutia
food.known_for: Simple, home-style North Indian vegetarian meals.

food.name: Sagar Gaire
food.known_for: Started as a cycle soup stall; now known for soups, triple-decker sandwiches and dosa.

food.name: 6 No. Hawkers Corner
food.known_for: Open-air snack corner: mawa bati, poha-jalebi, chaat and bhajiyas.

food.name: Hakeem's
food.known_for: Long-running local favourite for kebabs and biryani.

food.name: Za-aiqa, Noor-Us-Sabah Palace
food.known_for: Bhopali and Mughlai dishes in a palace hotel overlooking the lake.

stays.name: Jehan Numa Palace
stays.note: A 19th-century palace turned hotel with gardens. Close to the museums.

stays.name: Noor-Us-Sabah Palace
stays.note: Palace hotel on a hill above the Upper Lake.

stays.name: Taj Lakefront
stays.note: Modern luxury hotel on the lake shore next to Van Vihar.

stays.name: MPT Palash Residency
stays.note: Run by MP Tourism. Reliable, central and walkable to New Market.

stays.name: MP Nagar business hotels
stays.note: Mid-range chain hotels near DB Mall. Good transport links, little character.

stays.name: Hamidia Road budget hotels
stays.note: Cheapest beds, close to the station. Noisy; fine for a night in transit.
